ca_loaf_the.blurb: The Loaf is a large, uninterrupted block of granodiorite in the Alabama Hills near Lone Pine, part of the Western Wall Area. Eight lines climb its faces: six bolted and two traditional. Grades start around 5.8 and reach a single 5.12, though the bulk of the climbs fall between 5.9 and 5.10, which suits climbers comfortable on moderate sport leads. The routes follow long, clean faces rather than short boulder-style features. The walk in is a brief scramble through a gap between neighbouring boulders to the base of the formation.

ca_b1_boulder_2.blurb: B1 Boulder is a granite block in the Main Area at Horse Flats, a bouldering zone along the Angeles Crest Highway in the Angeles National Forest. Eight problems share the block, running from V0 up to V7. Five of them sit between V0 and V2, so a mixed group has warm-ups here, while a V4, a V6 and a V7 give stronger climbers something to work on. The boulder stands toward the upper end of the Main Area, which holds the densest cluster of problems at Horse Flats, and its face toward the trail carries thin patina plates.

ca_canyon_crest_road_boulder.blurb: A single boulder, roughly twelve feet tall, in the Arroyo Seco Boulders above Altadena in the Angeles National Forest. Eight problems start at V0, with three V0s, two V1s, a V2, a V3 and a V5, so most of the lines suit newer boulderers. Big holds make the block look straightforward, but the footholds are poor and the rounded, slopey top-out asks for care on the final moves. An easy walk-off leads down the back side. It is a short outing from the road rather than a destination.
ca_canyon_crest_road_boulder.parking_note: A small turnout on either side of Canyon Crest Road, about half a mile along it, puts you close to the boulder.
ca_canyon_crest_road_boulder.approach: Drop into the canyon from the turnout and follow it downstream to the boulder.

ca_clarksville_canyon.blurb: Clarksville Canyon is a bouldering sector of the Clarksville zone in Culp Valley, in San Diego County's desert country. It has eight problems, and they lean hard: a V4 and two V5s at the easy end, two V8s, two V10s and a V13 sit start at the top. Big boulders sit up or down the canyon after a walk of roughly a mile along a path, depending on how far you wander. This is a spot for strong boulderers rather than a first outing.

ca_black_star_canyon_bouldering.blurb: Black Star Canyon Bouldering lies in the Santa Ana Mountains on the eastern side of the Los Angeles Basin. Eight problems are spread among boulders beside the creek on the trail toward the waterfall, with some scrambling along the way. Grades run from V0 to a single V7: three V2s anchor the middle, with a V3 and two V4s above them. The first part of the hike is open to the sun, while the trees thicken once you reach the falls trail, giving the boulders plenty of shade.

ca_1_the_egg.blurb: The Egg is a small, freestanding boulder that serves as the landmark for the Third Turnout bouldering in Mill Creek Canyon, in the San Bernardino Mountains. Eight problems cover the block, and the grades stay low: two VB lines, a V0, two V1s, a V2 and a V3, with a single V5 on top. That makes it a friendly place for beginners and for children. Sand has built up around the base over time, so the boulder stands shorter than it once did. The walk is about five minutes, down into the wash, across the creek and a little way upstream.

ca_buck_rock.blurb: Buck Rock is a granodiorite dome high in the southern Sierra, topped by a fire lookout that is reached by stairs and looks out over Kings Canyon and the high country. The routes are steep, single-pitch lines on the southeast face, mostly bolted: four sport climbs between 5.10 and 5.11, a 5.8 top rope and a 5.10 trad line. Two boulder problems at V2 and V3 sit on blocks scattered downhill to the south. The crag is among the few mostly sport venues in the Sequoia and Kings Canyon region, and the climbing season runs through summer and fall.

ca_dollhouse_boulder.blurb: Dollhouse Boulder is one of several boulders in Valley of the Dolls, on Sugarloaf Mountain in Box Springs Mountain Reserve above Riverside. Eight problems cover the block, and the difficulty is almost uniformly low: seven are VB and one is V0, so it is a gentle stop for children and first-time boulderers. One face is split by three seams, and the setting gives views over the city. To reach it, hike partway up the valley trail, then turn onto the narrow side paths leading to the base.

_conflicts.ca_canyon_crest_road_boulder: Stored rock is sandstone; the parent page (https://mountainproject.com/area/107268701/arroyo-seco-boulders) says granite; the boulder's own page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/107268718/canyon-crest-road-boulder) names no rock.
